title: Readiness 4 · Generics through tracker
prompt: IReader<T> and two readers are supplied. Write two methods. public static async Task<T> ReadOrAsync<T>(IReader<T> reader, T fallback) returns the value the reader reads. When the reader throws InvalidOperationException, it returns the fallback. A value of 0 or an empty string is a real result. public static bool LastOrCheck(Func<List<int>, int, int> candidate) is a check for a candidate that should return the last item of a list, or the given fallback for an empty list. Return true for a correct candidate. Return false for a faulty one that returns the first item, and for one that returns 0 for an empty list whatever the fallback is.
hints: For ReadOrAsync, where does a failed read show up? For LastOrCheck, which inputs make each faulty candidate give a different answer?
A list with two different items exposes first versus last. An empty list with a fallback other than 0 exposes the second bug.
Await the read in a try and return fallback from catch (InvalidOperationException). In the check, compare candidate(list of 4 and 9, 0) with 9 and candidate(empty list, 7) with 7.
checks: Practice.LastOrCheck((items, fallback) => items.Count == 0 ? fallback : items[items.Count - 1]) == true
Practice.LastOrCheck((items, fallback) => items.Count == 0 ? fallback : items[0]) == false
checkLabels: The same method must work for a reader of strings.
An offline reader must give the fallback.
A value of 0 is a real result, not a failure.
A correct candidate must pass your check.
A candidate that returns the first item must fail your check.
A candidate that returns 0 for an empty list must fail your check.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Awaits the read with nothing to handle an offline reader.
Tests a list with one item, where first and last are the same.

feedback: For the reader, compare an offline reader with one that holds 0. For the check, find an input where each faulty candidate gives a different answer from a correct one.
